2026-07-25 cross-spec review amendments applied to requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md; approvals retained. (1) BLOCKING: Req 3.1's premise was false as designed -- load-channels defined heart-rate intensity as the impulse ratio, the square of the power/pace intensity for the same load, coinciding only at 1.0 at threshold, so the divergence flag read DIVERGENT on easy sessions where the channels agreed and AGREED near threshold. load-channels Req 1.11/5.11 now define one shared semantic (HR intensity = sqrt(impulse_ratio); load == hours x intensity^2 x 100 within 1e-9 relative on every channel). Req 3.1 restated against that invariant; new Req 3.9 adds a sub-threshold agreement regression that a threshold-only fixture cannot fail. (2) Ruling on divergence_max_intensity_delta: it CANNOT be justified from the corpus evidence in this spec -- the 74-file measurement computed no activity on which two channels both produced a value, so there is no agreement distribution to set a tolerance against. The value stays at 0.20 (substituting another unmeasured number would be inventing one) but its provenance is downgraded from measured to provisional; new Req 6.11 and an extended Req 6.10 require an unvalidated default to say so and to name the measurement that would settle it, recorded as a typed PROVISIONAL_DEFAULTS entry in qa/sources.py. An open question is filed with it: an absolute delta is scale-dependent under a squared load relation, and the same measurement would settle whether the comparison should be relative. (3) BLOCKING: the import-cycle invariant is withdrawn -- the cycle never materialised in the traced graph and its cause (ProfileView.load_settings) is removed by training-load Amendment 3's per-pass LoadContext(activity_date, settings). load/qa/__init__.py is restored to an ordinary initializer exporting evaluate_flags; the import-order regression test and tests/load/qa/test_import_order.py are deleted; staleness reads context.settings.benchmark_staleness_days and context.activity_date. (4) FITDOCS_MEASURED is now defined by load-channels task 1.1; task 1.2's enum edit and its edit of tests/load/channels/test_sources.py are removed, leaving this feature's footprint entirely inside its own package. (5) Provenance defects fixed: uniqueness restated over Citation.key and Divergence.behavior (Divergence deliberately has no key), matching load-channels' resolution; the divergence table's 'five' corrected to six. (6) Brief corrections carried into spec text: new Req 3.10 records that the '19 versus 241' anecdote could not be located and justifies nothing; Req 4.5 extended to withdraw the brief's framing of Efficiency Factor as a signal. (7) The future-dated-benchmark guard now carries its rationale explicitly -- it is the seam that makes athlete-benchmarks' raising benchmark_age and threshold-load Req 1.7's never-raises simultaneously satisfiable, and must not be deleted as dead code. Counts after amendment: 76 acceptance criteria across 9 requirements (was 73; +3.9, +3.10, +6.11), 18 task entries in 4 phases (unchanged), 10 design components (unchanged, with CalculatorIntegration and PublicSurfacePin now claimed by task boundaries). Mechanical re-verification: every AC appears in design.md, in the traceability table and in a task _Requirements:_ line; no phantom IDs; task numbering sequential; all _Depends:_ edges valid; the (P) wave (2.1, 2.3, 2.4, 2.5) still touches disjoint modules and disjoint test modules.

2026-07-25 second cross-spec review round applied to requirements.md, design.md and tasks.md; approvals retained. (A) BLOCKING, superseding amendment (3) above: this spec's report of a surviving import cycle (fitdocs.load.types -> fitdocs.load.settings -> fitdocs.load.qa/__init__ -> fitdocs.load.qa.flags -> fitdocs.load.types partial -> ImportError) was CORRECT and the reviewer reproduced it -- worse than reported, since src/fitdocs/load/__init__.py:19 imports registry -> types, so it fails on every entry point, not only when load.types is imported first. The mitigation this spec proposed (a lazy module-level __getattr__ in load/qa/__init__.py) was REJECTED in favour of one of the two clean alternatives it had itself named: training-load now adds `if TYPE_CHECKING: from fitdocs.load.settings import LoadSettings` to src/fitdocs/load/types.py, putting settings.py back above types.py, restoring that module's shipped 'no imports from other fitdocs.load.* modules' invariant, and letting every sub-package import load.types freely. A future load/channels/ edge importing fitdocs.load.types breaks the lazy version and passes the TYPE_CHECKING version, which is why the workaround was not kept. Consequently: the 'One residual edge survives' design section is replaced by a record of the finding and the upstream ruling; the directory-structure comment, the FlagAssembly export note and the design's amendment summary describe an ordinary EAGER initializer; task 1.1 creates an eager initializer with no import restriction; task 3.1 re-exports evaluate_flags with a plain `from .flags import evaluate_flags`; task 1.3's in-process import assertion in tests/load/test_settings.py is DELETED rather than duplicated -- an in-process re-import after the test module's own top-level imports is a sys.modules cache hit and proves nothing, and training-load owns the single fresh-interpreter guard by extending the existing subprocess check at tests/test_public_api.py:353 to cover `import fitdocs.load.qa` and `import fitdocs.load.types`. (B) The src/fitdocs/load/settings.py ownership pin is now recorded, which this spec alone had been missing: the module belongs to training-load task 3.1, which pins load_load_settings(document, settings_file) -> LoadSettings, LoadSettingsError(SettingsError) and DEFAULT_LOAD_SETTINGS, ignoring unknown keys AND unknown sub-tables so siblings extend the one dataclass and the one reader. tasks.md's prerequisite bullet moved the module off athlete-benchmarks (which still owns benchmark_staleness_days as a member), and task 1.3's stop-condition now sequences training-load, not athlete-benchmarks. Counts after this round: 76 acceptance criteria across 9 requirements (unchanged -- removing the workaround changed no criterion), 18 task entries in 4 phases (unchanged -- no task added or removed; three task bodies edited). Nothing in this spec now contradicts the ruling. Mechanical re-verification re-run: 76 unique criteria, no duplicates, every ID present in design.md and in a task _Requirements:_ line, no phantom IDs, sub-task numbering sequential within each phase, all _Depends:_ edges resolve, the (P) wave is still 2.1/2.3/2.4/2.5 over disjoint source and test modules.
